utterances.speaker: C
utterances.text: As the chief mentioned, you may remember, throughout 2022, staff worked with a consultant from crisis consulting to research the feasibility of San Rafael having an alternative response team incorporated into the city's emergency response system. On January 17, 2023, Council approved the City Manager to enter into a three year agreement professional services agreement with Petaluma People Services to operate a specialized assistance for everyone team. Also known as the SAFE Team. The SAFE Team is responsible for responding to calls for service involving community members in crisis through trauma and informed de escalation, conflict resolution, welfare checks, low level medical aid and substance abuse counseling. The community is able to access the SAFE team through 911 emergency, a dedicated telephone line or through the San Rafael Police Department's non emergency telephone number. The goal of the SAFE Team is to address people in crisis prevention and intervention to our most vulnerable community members. The team is comprised of civilian crisis counselors and emergency medical technicians who operate eight in the morning, morning to 8pm seven days a week, 365 days a year. The SAFE team currently has 10 crisis counselors, an emergency medical technician, one part time navigator, one part time director, and one program manager. In November 2023, the SAFE team took delivery of the new Ford Transit van as depicted here in the slide.

utterances.speaker: C
utterances.text: Over the past 10 months, the SAFE team has responded to 2,693 calls for service. 50% of the calls for service involve public assists. Typically, these types of calls for service involve the unhoused community and can range from connecting someone to services providing food, water, water or clothing. Harm reduction, assessing someone acting unusual or for subjects blocking driveways or entrances, the second most common call type handled by the SAFE Team are welfare checks. Welfare checks typically are initiated by community members, social workers such as adult, adult Protective services, child protective services, hospital staff, family members or other parties requesting the SAFE Team check on a member of the San Rafael community. The reason for the welfare checks could be because the person has not heard from the community member for some time and they suffer from a medical, psychiatric or physical condition or the person miss scheduled appointments walked away from the hospital against medical advice following a crisis, trauma or serious accident.

utterances.speaker: C
utterances.text: Based on a review of the monthly Calls for Service staff projects, the SAFE team will handle approximately 3,200 calls for service since their inception. This represents approximately 7% of SRPD's calls for service. San Rafael PD dispatch classifies all calls for service into three priority categories. Priority one equals in progress potential life threatening emergencies priority two. Two is equal to serious crime or incident with potential for escalation or harm such as a mental health crisis, suicidal subject with no weapons and Priority three incidents involve no suspect activity in progress, non emergencies or no likelihood for injury or cold crime reports since March 27, 2023, when the SAFE team began handling calls for service, they have responded to priority two and priority three type of calls. They have responded within 22 minutes from the time the call is initiated to when the SAFE Team is dispatched. Comparatively, all other calls for service where only police responded, the response time was 37 minutes for priority two and priority three type of calls. Even though they handle only 7% of the overall call volume, they're responding faster than if those calls were only handled by the police. Not to mention the police love having the Safety Team.

utterances.speaker: C
utterances.text: The implementation of the SAFE team was a contributing factor in the police department lowering our response time to priority one call types. Priority one response times went from seven minutes in 2022 to five minutes in 2023. SAFE team freed up valuable resources to make officers available to respond to higher priority calls. Since the inception of the Safe Team, staff has spent a total of $591,000 on the Safe Safe Team team personnel expenses, vehicle purchase, upfitting, office space, reorganization and equipment. This is about 68% of the budget and we are currently operating a little bit below budget. Staff has allocated state opioid funding, one time funding from the County, American Rescue Plan funding, cannabis revenue, AB109 realignment and Marin County Major Crimes Task Force funding to cover the SAFE Team expenses. The SAFE Team has assisted community members with securing housing, alleviated public safety resources, making officers paramount medic and firefighters available for other priority one details. They've also assisted community members, become medication compliant, connected community members with psychiatric services, and assisted in de escalating events. Currently, the SAFE team only operates 12 hours per day from 8 in the morning to 8pm they are not available to people who may be in crisis for the other 12 hours. As a result, SRPD officers or the Marin County Mobile Crisis Unit are dispatched to handle these incidents. The SAFE Team has saved a considerable amount of officers and paramedics time through jail diversions, mental health evaluations and emergency department deferrals. In 2024 and 2025, staff will be looking for additional funding strategies to continue operation. Staff will be exploring state and federal grants, community partnership and other funding options for program sustainability. Staff will also evaluate the viability of expansion to 18 hour or 24 hour service. In 2022, Crisis Consulting projected an 18 hour staffing model would cost an estimated $915,000 per year.
